newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's opposition ends parliament boycott.
newsitem.headline: Albania's opposition ends parliament boycott.

text.p: Albania's opposition Democratic Party returned to parliament on Wednesday after a three-week boycott in protest against the handling of the election that toppled them from power.

Former president Sali Berisha, the Democratic Party leader, remained defiant in his attitude towards the new Socialist-led government, accusing it of bearing political grudges and not living up to promises given for Albania's return to normality.
The collapse of bogus investment pyramid schemes earlier this year triggered months of rebellion and anarchy with more than 1,500 deaths, leading to the downfall of Berisha's right-wing government.
"While we shall welcome what you achieve, we shall denounce what you do not in order to shorten the days of your governing violence," Berisha told the assembly.

Fatos Nano's five-party coalition government has vowed to introduce sweeping institutional changes and to depoliticise the civil service through the reform of the financial system, the police and the army.
